schematicStates.fact: North Korean forces invaded south across the 38th parallel on 25 June 1950.
By early September 1950, Republic of Korea and UN forces defended the southeastern Busan perimeter.

After the Incheon landing and counteroffensive, Republic of Korea and UN forces advanced far north before the major Chinese counteroffensive in late November 1950. The line is an intentionally simplified mainland core-front view, not a continuous archival battlefield front.
Chinese and North Korean forces recaptured Seoul on 4 January 1951; UN and Republic of Korea forces withdrew south before recovering ground later in 1951.

The armistice signed on 27 July 1953 ended active fighting with a front near the 38th parallel. The existing simplified present inter-Korean boundary is used as a visual approximation of the final stalemate, not the surveyed Military Demarcation Line.
